login.title: Sign in
login.heading: Sign in
mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.heading: Two-factor authentication
mfa.lostdevice: Lost your device? Enter one of your recovery codes instead.
emailotp.title: Email sign-in codes
emailotp.done.heading: Email codes are on
emailotp.done.body: You will be asked for a code from this address when you sign in.
emailotp.done.hint: This is the weakest of the second factors we offer, because account recovery already goes to your email — anybody with your mailbox can do both. An authenticator app or a passkey is stronger, and you can add one at any time.
emailotp.check.heading: Check your email
emailotp.start.body: We will send a code to this address each time you sign in.
emailotp.start.hint: An authenticator app is stronger: your email is also how your account is recovered, so a code sent there protects you from a stolen password but not from a stolen mailbox.
smsotp.title: Text message codes
smsotp.enrolled.note: A text message is the weakest second factor available here: moving a phone number to a new SIM needs no technical attack, only a convincing phone call to a mobile operator. An authenticator app or a passkey is stronger, and you can have both.
smsotp.sent: A code was sent to {Number}. Enter it to finish.
smsotp.verify.note: This factor is not active until the code comes back. That is what proves the number is yours and not a typo.
smsotp.number.label: Mobile number, with the country code
smsotp.number.note: Start with a + and the country code. Without it the number cannot be dialled, and guessing wrong sends your codes to somebody else.
smsotp.unavailable: Text messages are not available on this server.
enrol.title: Set up two-factor authentication
enrol.scan: Scan this with your authenticator app:
enrol.typekey: Type this key into your authenticator app instead:
enrol.openlink: Or open this link on the device with your authenticator app.
recovery.title: Your recovery codes
recovery.heading: Two-factor authentication is on
recovery.save: Save these recovery codes now. Each one works once, and this is the only time they can be shown — only hashes are stored, so nobody can retrieve them for you later.
recovery.hint: Keep them somewhere other than the device with your authenticator app. If you lose both, you lose the account.
done.title: Password changed
done.heading: Your password has been changed
done.body: Every signed-in session was ended, on every device.
cancelled.title: Reset cancelled
cancelled.heading: That reset has been cancelled
cancelled.body: The link will not work. Nothing about your account has changed.
cancelled.hint: If you did not request the reset, your password is still safe, but somebody knows your address. Consider turning on two-factor authentication.
recover.title: Reset your password
recover.hint: We will email every address on the account, and the reset will only become usable after a short delay — so a request you did not make cannot go through without you having a chance to stop it.
sent.title: Check your email
sent.body: If an account matches what you entered, we have emailed reset instructions to every address on it.
sent.hint: The email includes a link to cancel, in case the request was not yours. Cancelling needs no sign-in.
reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.pending: This reset is not usable yet. It becomes available at {When} — about {Wait} from now.
reset.pending.hint: The wait is deliberate: it is the window in which a reset you did not ask for can still be cancelled from the link in your email.
reset.submit: Set password and sign out everywhere
changepw.title: Choose a new password
changepw.help: A few unrelated words make a password that is easy to remember and hard to guess. Length does more than symbols do.
signup.title: Create your account
signup.invitefixed: This invitation is for this address.
signup.passwordhint: At least 8 characters. You can add a passkey once you are in.
signupdone.title: Account created
logout.title: Sign out?
logout.heading: Sign out?
logout.body: An application asked to sign you out. Confirm that this is what you want.
fclogout.title: Signing out…
fclogout.heading: Signing you out

fclogout.progress.one: Signing you out of {n} application. This page will continue automatically.
fclogout.progress.other: Signing you out of {n} applications. This page will continue automatically.

backchannel.title: Sign-in requests
backchannel.intro: An application has asked to sign in as you. Approve it only if you started it.
backchannel.binding: Reference shown on the other device:
consent.title: Authorize {Client}
consent.heading: {Client} wants access to your account
consent.operation: And to perform this specific operation:
device.title: Connect a device
device.done.heading: Device connected
device.done.body: You can put this away and go back to the device.
device.denied.heading: Request refused
device.denied.body: Nothing was granted. If you did not start this, somebody else may have asked you to enter that code — it is worth telling whoever runs your systems.
device.confirm.heading: Allow this device?
device.confirm.body: {ClientName} is asking to sign in as you on a device.
device.confirm.warning: Only continue if you started this yourself, on a device in front of you. Nobody legitimate will ask you to enter a code they sent you.
device.enter: Enter the code shown on your device.
connected.title: Connected applications
connected.none: No application has been granted access to your account.
sessions.title: Your sessions
sessions.none: You have no other active sessions.
sessions.how.mfa: Signed in with a password and a second factor
sessions.how.multifactor: Signed in with more than one factor
sessions.endcurrent: End this session (signs you out here)
accountpw.title: Change your password
accountpw.endsothers: Changing your password ends every session, so you will sign in again with the new one.
reccodes.title: Recovery codes
reccodes.nofactor: Recovery codes back up a second factor, and you have not set one up yet.

reccodes.remaining.zero: You have no unused recovery codes left.
reccodes.remaining.one: You have {n} unused recovery code left.
reccodes.remaining.other: You have {n} unused recovery codes left.

reccodes.explain: Each code works once. Keep them somewhere other than the device with your authenticator app.
reccodes.replaces: Generating new codes cancels your current ones, so any you have written down will stop working.
portal.title: Your applications
portal.empty: No applications have been set up yet.
portal.empty.hint: An administrator registers one with signari client create.
portal.nolaunch: You can use this, but no launch address is configured. Ask an administrator to set -launch-url.
portal.blocked.heading: Not available to you
portal.blocked.hint: Listed with the reason, so you know what to ask for rather than having to open a ticket to find out.
account.title: Your account
account.heading: Sign-in methods
account.note: Adding a provider here is the only way to link one to this account. We never link on a matching email address alone.
account.none: No external sign-in providers are configured.
racindex.title: Remote access
racindex.notconfigured: Remote access is not configured on this server. No SIGNARI_GUACD_ADDR is set, so nothing can be connected to.
racindex.none: There are no machines you can reach.
racindex.none.hint: If you expect to see something here, ask an administrator whether the connection requires a group you are not in.
umaclaims.title: Confirm this request
umaclaims.heading: {ClientName} is asking on your behalf
umaclaims.note: Confirming tells {ResourceServer} who you are. It does not grant access on its own: whoever owns this decides that.
err.title: Sign-in error
federr.title: Sign-in could not be completed
samlerr.title: Sign-in request refused
samlerr.heading: This sign-in request was refused
reason.breached: Your password has appeared in a known data breach since you chose it, so it needs to be changed before you continue.
reason.migratedbreach: The password you brought from your previous provider appears in a known data breach, so it needs to be changed before you continue.
reason.administrator: An administrator has asked you to choose a new password.
scope.offline_access: Stay signed in and access your account while you are away
error.totp.mismatch: That code did not match. Check your authenticator app and try again.
error.reset.expired: That link is not valid or has expired.
error.invite.invalid: That invitation link is not valid. It may have been used already, or expired. Ask whoever invited you for a new one.
error.captcha.incomplete: That challenge was not completed. Please try again.
bridge.title: Signing you in…
bridge.noscript: JavaScript is disabled. Continue to complete signing in.
mail.signincode.subject: Your sign-in code
mail.confirmaddress.subject: Confirm this address for sign-in codes
mail.recovery.requested.subject: Password reset requested
mail.recovery.requested.body:
Someone asked to reset the password for your account.

If this was you, the reset becomes available in {Wait}:

  {ResetURL}

If it was NOT you, cancel it now -- no sign-in needed:

  {CancelURL}

The delay is deliberate. It exists so that a reset you did not ask for cannot happen without you having a chance to stop it.

This message was sent to every address on the account, including ones the request did not come from.
sms.recovery.requested: A password reset was requested on your account. If this was not you, check your email now for a one-tap link to cancel it -- no sign-in needed.
mail.password.changed.subject: Your password was changed
mail.password.changed.body:
Your account password has just been changed, and every signed-in session was ended.

If this was not you, reset it again immediately and contact your administrator.
sms.password.changed: Your account password was just changed and all sessions ended. If this was not you, reset it again now and contact your administrator.
mail.passkey.added.subject: A new passkey was added to your account
mail.passkey.added.body:
A passkey named {Label} was added to your account on {When}.

If you added it, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT add it, someone else may have had access to your account. Sign in, remove the passkey you do not recognise, and change your password. If you cannot sign in, contact support at {Support}.
sms.passkey.added: A new passkey ({Label}) was just added to your account. If this was not you, sign in and remove it, then change your password.
mail.passkey.removed.subject: A passkey was removed from your account
mail.passkey.removed.body:
The passkey {Label} was removed from your account on {When}.

If you removed it, there is nothing to do.

If you did NOT remove it, someone else may have access to your account. Sign in, check the passkeys listed there, and change your password. If you cannot sign in, contact support at {Support}.
sms.passkey.removed: The passkey {Label} was just removed from your account. If this was not you, sign in and change your password.
mail.recoverycodes.replaced.subject: Your recovery codes were replaced
mail.recoverycodes.replaced.body:
Your account's recovery codes were just regenerated. The previous set no longer works.

If you did not do this, someone else may have access to your account: change your password and review your sign-in methods.
sms.recoverycodes.replaced: Your account's recovery codes were just replaced. If this was not you, change your password now.
